title: 16-Layer Quarter-Wave Initialized Stack with ±8% Bounded Optimization
scientific_hypothesis: Initializing layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness for the 10.5 μm central wavelength of the high-emissivity band, then optimizing within ±8% bounds, will reduce search entropy and recover or exceed the iteration_01 best score of 0.8903 by maintaining constructive interference in the target band while suppressing the 3-5 μm band.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack initialization provides a physically motivated starting point that reduces optimization search space while allowing local refinement for spectral shaping.
proposed_topology: Air | [HfO2 | SiO2] × 8 | Si substrate (16 finite layers, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: layer thicknesses (16 variables, initialized at quarter-wave values for 10.5 μm, bounded ±8%)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean absorptance in 8000-13000 nm band
Minimize mean absorptance in 3000-5000 nm band
Maintain total layer count at exactly 16
manufacturing_considerations: Quarter-wave thicknesses in IR range are fabrication-feasible (approximately 1000-1500 nm per layer)
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance/transmittance bands centered at design wavelength
Kirchhoff's law relates absorptance to emissivity for thermal equilibrium
Transfer Matrix Method accurately models multilayer interference in frequency domain
expected_advantages: Reduced search entropy compared to uniform/random initialization
Physical motivation for initial thickness values
More layers than prior 12-layer routes may improve spectral selectivity
known_risks: Quarter-wave initialization may trap optimizer in local minimum
16 layers may increase fabrication complexity without proportional performance gain
HfO2/SiO2 index contrast in mid-IR may be insufficient for ideal spectral shaping
execution_request_english: Optimize a 16-layer planar dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2 (16 finite layers total). Initialize all HfO2 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 10500 nm central wavelength, initialize all SiO2 layers at quarter-wave optical thickness for 10500 nm. Apply ±8% thickness bounds around initial values during optimization. Target: maximize mean absorptance in 8000-13000 nm band, minimize mean absorptance in 3000-5000 nm band. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized or both TE/TM. Materials: HfO2 and SiO2 from material registry with IR refractive index data. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3000-5000 nm, 8000-13000 nm. soft objectives: high emissivity in 8000-13000 nm; low emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high emissivity in 3000-5000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 24.
revision_reason: Increased layer count from 12 to 16 to test whether additional degrees of freedom improve spectral contrast; quarter-wave initialization with ±8% bounds per feedback directive to reduce search entropy compared to prior uniform/broad initialization approaches.
